html:
The Granada War was a series of campaigns from 1482 to 1492 in the south of today's Spain. Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon conquered the Emirate of Granada, the last Muslim state in Iberia. It ended with the siege and surrender of the city of Granada on 2 January 1492.

Granada had survived for 250 years, often by paying tribute to Castile. The marriage of Isabella and Ferdinand joined the two largest Christian kingdoms, and they set out to finish the Reconquista. Heavy cannon broke the walls of hill towns that once took years to starve out. The emirate was also split by a civil war inside its ruling family, which the Christians fed by backing the young emir Boabdil. Ronda fell in 1485 and Málaga in 1487. In 1491 the Christian army camped outside Granada itself. After eight months Boabdil gave up the city and the Alhambra.

Nearly eight centuries of Muslim rule in Iberia were over. The treaty promised Muslims their religion, but the promise was soon broken. In the same year the monarchs ordered the expulsion of the Jews and agreed to pay for the voyage of Columbus.
